scope: Initial NDIS 5.1 i386 Ethernet driver for RTL8125A/B, MTU 1500, one queue, software checksums, copied DMA buffers. Linux identifies the host card as RTL8125B XID 641; native ReactOS physical identification remains pending.
scoring: Implementation measures source code only; tests never add or subtract implementation credit. Each source milestone has four explicit code criteria. Preserve original four acceptance gates and original weights separately. Code progress weights use M00–M09 original units (96 total), normalized to 100%; M10 is validation-only with zero code weight. Overall code percent = sum(original weight units × code percent) / 96. Documentation has no code weight.
completion_policy: Mark code criteria complete after source review; track build/model/guest/physical evidence separately. Acceptance gates retain their original evidence requirements. User explicitly revised implementation scoring on 2026-10-24 to exclude testing.

os_changes.dma: No ReactOS patch planned: existing DMA adapter and common-buffer APIs support the copying design; actual integration remains to be verified.
os_changes.interrupts: The actual PCI configuration advertises INTA (evidence/linux-config.json). No OS patch is planned if assigned INTx works. If the platform requires MSI and the target ReactOS stack cannot deliver it, a separate PCI/HAL/NDIS change is a prerequisite. The advertised pin alone does not prove routing.
os_changes.limits: Copying adds CPU/memory bandwidth cost. Full 2.5 Gb/s throughput is unmeasured. Do not change OS source merely because ScatterGatherListSize is a placeholder.
os_changes.ndis_lifecycle: Operational use requires all three ordered canonical patches: Halt callback context, wrapper callback rundown, device-power IRP bridge. The complete patched NDIS module compiled/linked in an owned copy; the external SDK and running guests remain unchanged. No scatter/gather/common-buffer DMA API patch is needed.
